prompt: An exponential function $f$ satisfies $f(1) = 6$, $f(2) = 18$, and $f(3) = 54$. What is the value of $f(0)$?
hint: Find the constant ratio between consecutive outputs.

hints.text: Find the constant ratio between consecutive outputs.
$18 \div 6 = 3$ and $54 \div 18 = 3$, so the function triples each step.

learningObjective: Extend an exponential pattern backwards to its initial value.
explanation: Consecutive outputs have a constant ratio: $\dfrac{18}{6} = \dfrac{54}{18} = 3$. That constant ratio is what makes the function exponential.
Stepping forward multiplies by $3$, so stepping backward divides by $3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Linear or exponential? Check differences and ratios
steps: Differences here are $12$ and $36$ — not constant, so the function is not linear.
Ratios are $3$ and $3$ — constant, so it is exponential.
Running both checks takes ten seconds and settles every "which model fits this table" question on the test.
